approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecules from score-ranked accepted survivors by connected-fragment crossover or local graph edits. It builds a fresh pool for each batch, fits a Tanimoto fingerprint Gaussian process to all earlier accepted observations, and selects molecules by correlated posterior function draws. One growth move appends a single atom to an available hydrogen-bearing site; that site can currently be carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus or sulfur regardless of which element is added.
approach.novelty: Make halogen addition use carbon attachment sites. If the original growth draw would attach fluorine, chlorine or bromine to a heteroatom, redirect that same one-atom addition to an available carbon site; if none exists, let the existing bounded mutation retry continue. This preserves the source molecule's heavy-atom connections and the chosen halogen while changing its new bond context. Earlier siblings changed which accepted parents breed or survive. This Child instead changes one local growth channel, and uses explicit attachment chemistry rather than the corpus-occurrence rule tried in a different lineage.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent's accepted-only fingerprint posterior consistently selects from fresh graph-evolution pools, but its append operator chooses an H-bearing C/N/O/P/S anchor before drawing the appended element and permits direct heteroatom-halogen growth. A read-only audit of its complete logged seed panel finds 215 new N/O-halogen bonds among 8,276 pooled descendants whose sole realized operation is append_atom, and 16 among 602 such emitted descendants; every one of those 215 source graphs also had eligible carbon anchors. These are logged source/product bond-count differences on a single-operation channel, not inferred scores for unused molecules. The Parent's molecular assessment identifies N/O-halogen motifs even in high-scoring families and shows nearby carbon-bound alternatives; its overall 565/4,350 best-parent beats and mean child-minus-best-parent deficit -0.100493 leave room to improve local proposal chemistry. The four feedback-memory siblings changed core allocation, survivor retention, historical parent credit or partner similarity, but all lowered paired macro means while leaving graph production intact. Corpus-support gating elsewhere also retained locally supported N-Cl chemistry, so empirical local occurrence does not answer this attachment-specific question.
hypothesis: Redirect halogen append mutations from heteroatom anchors to uniformly sampled eligible carbon anchors, preserving the selected halogen and single-atom growth.

finding_summary.headline: Carbon-directed halogen growth removed its reactive-bond channel, but final scores fell.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment establishes that an attachment rule can remove a specific reactive-bond introduction while preserving the surrounding graph, without solving the broader chemistry problem. The rule changed a small evaluated channel: 22 of 4,350 proposals carried its redirected edit in their immediate breeding history. Meanwhile, 56 emitted N-halogen-containing molecules and 31 O-halogen-containing molecules had no such motif in either original generating parent, demonstrating introductions through the unchanged operators. Other products already had that motif available in their parents; their exact bond ancestry cannot be inferred from motif presence alone.

Carbon attachment itself remains chemically permissive. Four redirected pool products acquired a carbonyl-halide connection and three an imine-carbon-halide connection; none of those seven was evaluated. The full selected stream also contained more carbonyl/imine halides, while the molecular assessment still found strained small rings, reactive decorations, oversized repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. These observations narrow the next chemistry question to attachment environment and other introduction routes, rather than treating all carbon-bound halogens as robust alternatives. The simultaneous increase in core coverage and parent-beating events with a lower final best score also shows that these intermediate gains do not establish endpoint benefit. The altered stochastic search paths and posterior selection do not identify a causal score penalty for the removed, unscored attachment alternatives.
finding_summary.results:
The intended attachment change reached both pools and evaluation. All 489 halogen draws with a heteroatom anchor and available carbon support were redirected, sanitized and reconstructed as the same selected halogen attached by one new C-halogen bond. Every old heavy atom and bond was preserved, and all 489 direct products retained the source ring core. One further opportunity had no carbon site and correctly continued the bounded retry. The successful edits supplied 482 distinct pool descendants and 22 evaluated descendants; 19 of those ended with the append, while three underwent later edits.

The direct channel produced no new heteroatom-halogen bonds. The Parent’s single-append pool products had added 160 N-halogen, 55 O-halogen and 25 other heteroatom-halogen bonds; its emitted single-append products added 16 N-halogen and three other heteroatom-halogen bonds. Across all evaluated proposals, molecules containing N-halogen decreased from 572 to 535 and O-halogen from 441 to 173, but both remained common. Ring-core identities across the full emitted stream increased from 2,266 to 2,409; no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry appeared.

All fifteen tasks completed the same 300-call budgets. Novel pool yield rose from 92.05% to 92.55%, and accepted molecules beating their best generating parent increased from 565 to 605. Among the 22 redirected descendants, two beat their best parent, one improved the incumbent and none was a final task/seed best. Mean final Top-1 nevertheless fell from 0.544374 to 0.539209, a paired change of -0.005165; seed changes were -0.011685, -0.020367 and +0.016558. The mechanism is confirmed, with negative and uneven endpoint utility.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and aryl amines coexist with reactive bonds, strained small rings, and oversized repeated assemblies
molecular.overall_character: The supplied current and parent trajectories cover every task and seed. Current proposals span compact aryl amides, saturated nitrogen rings, fused cyclic diones, and much larger repeated heteroaromatic assemblies. Ring and aromatic content are rich: the digest's ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9736 to 0.992, and aromatic-token presence rates from 0.9471 to 0.992. These are molecule-level SMILES readings, not aromatic atom fractions or evidence of feasible ring geometry. Halogen-token rates vary from 0.1655 to 0.9943, while explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero throughout. Neutral drawings include potentially basic amines. The conventional aryl dione family shows that plausible medicinal chemistry is accessible, but other leaders carry acid chlorides, aldehydes, nitroso groups, direct nitrogen-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence, or highly unsaturated small rings. Distinct seed families provide moderate structural diversity; numerous unique strings also represent close decoration variants or duplication of existing ring systems. Relative to the parent, the chemistry moves between families without consistently removing these liabilities. The supplied scores establish structural associations, not a unique absent pharmacophore or synthetic feasibility.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact, densely bridged aromatic systems carrying an N-methyl arylamide. The best contains benzene and pyridine rings, an oxygen/methylene/nitrogen bridge, and a sulfur-containing unsaturated ring; neighboring leaders exchange the aryl nitrogen, aryl halogen, bridge atom, or sulfur bond order. Other seeds produce more recognizable fused heteroaryl amides and benzene-annulated, highly unsaturated small rings. Thus there is abundant ring chemistry, rather than a shortage of molecular size: ring and aromatic presence rates are 0.9736 and 0.9713, with mean SMILES length 45.7. Ordinary amides and heteroaryl substituents look synthetically recognizable, but the multiply bridged connectivity and some unsaturated small-ring products need much more scrutiny.
liabilities: The sulfur cumulene with bracketed SH is an unusual chemical endpoint, despite its high supplied score.
Several final benzene-annulated unsaturated small rings have substantial geometric and electronic strain concerns.
Compact bridged topology does not by itself provide a credible synthesis, and late proposals still discard nearly all of the productive architecture.
missing_features: Matched simpler ring systems retaining the leading pyridylamide and heteroatom spacing are not established among the supplied leaders.
Stable sulfur and bridge alternatives are only partially represented; the near-leading cumulated sulfur structure leaves chemical stability unresolved.
Stereochemically specified versions of substituted bridge or ring variants are absent even when their connectivity can support stereoisomers.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyridyl N-methyl amide reaches 0.468900; the otherwise close fluorophenyl amide is 0.425708, and the unusual cumulated sulfur analogue is 0.457660. Within this local family, the aryl heteroatom arrangement matters and the unusual sulfur bonding does not improve the supplied score. Small fragments such as acetylene and methane score zero; the final methylfluoropyridine scores about 1.42e-11, so an aromatic ring alone is insufficient. A final indole-like arylamide scores 0.230346, whereas a different strained, annulated small-ring arylamide scores 0.388678; their multiple structural differences do not prove that strain is beneficial. The current seed-0 maximum is above the parent's 0.446352 and retains its compact bridged N/O-aromatic character while changing the carbonyl connection and sulfur content. Other current seed maxima are below their respective parent maxima, so the same chemical movement is not repeated across seeds.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest molecular population by SMILES length, with mean 95.2 and maximum 227. Almost every proposal has aromatic and ring tokens, both at 0.992. One recurring family links several nitrogen-rich aromatic diones through substituted heteroaryl connections and unsaturated chains. The best molecule is more compact than those repeated assemblies but remains a complex fused aza/oxygen carbonyl system, connected through an N-O bond to a fluorinated heteroaromatic ring bearing a brominated thioether side chain and a carbon-bound bromonitroso substituent. Final molecules include repeated ester-linked azaaromatics, additional nitroso groups, and N-bromo acylated enamines. These are chemically elaborate structures with substantial route and stability questions.
liabilities: The leading bromonitroso substituent combines a reactive nitroso group with carbon-bound bromine; it should not be read as an ordinary nitro substituent.
Imidoyl halides, direct N-bromination, and N-O connections complicate stability and synthesis.
Repeated dione assemblies add size, unsaturated chains, and many connecting bonds without a consistent supplied-score advantage.
missing_features: Comparably connected but compact heteroaromatic carbonyl structures with stable peripheral bonds are insufficiently represented among the highest supplied scores.
Matched removal of nitroso, direct N-halogen, and imidoyl-halide functionality is not demonstrated while holding the main ring architecture constant.
Simple connecting groups that preserve the useful heteroaromatic arrangement without duplicating complete dione systems remain a visible gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact bromonitroso/thioether structure scores 0.608446. Several much larger repeated-dione molecules tie at 0.603906: exchanging an imidoyl chlorine for bromine, or shortening one unsaturated side chain to ethyl, does not change that supplied score. A final molecule joining substantial portions of two complex aromatic systems falls to 0.579001, while a smaller thioether/carbonyl heterocycle without the bromonitroso group scores 0.588747. These examples support complete heteroaromatic/carbonyl assemblies over isolated fragments, but do not establish a benefit from repeated growth or a requirement for the reactive groups. Methane and vinyl bromide both sit at the 0.5 floor. The parent's best seed-1 structure scored 0.632470 and also carried problematic oxygen-halogen chemistry; the current maximum is lower and replaces that particular chemistry with other liabilities rather than demonstrating their resolution.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring family combines methoxyfluorophenyl and chlorophenyl groups with potentially basic saturated nitrogen rings, including pyrrolidine, piperidine, and expanded diaza rings. Enamine or related unsaturated connections organize these groups, often alongside chloromethyl, aldehyde, or acid-chloride substituents. The leader additionally carries an aryl amino group. Other seeds generate bridged amine cages and oxygen-bridged aromatic structures with strongly constrained small-ring connectivity. Aromatic, ring, and halogen presence rates are 0.9851, 0.9908, and 0.9943; mean SMILES length is 68.7. The aryl-amine building blocks are recognizable, but the reactive appendages and some fused topology make the actual outputs substantially less straightforward than conventional aryl cyclic amines.
liabilities: Acid chlorides are reactive acylating functionalities, rather than routine stable amide or ketone decorations.
Enamines, aldehydes, and activated alkyl chlorides introduce stability or reactivity concerns despite high scores.
Late oxygen-bridged small rings and N-bromo analogues add separate geometry and bond-stability concerns.
Multiple neutral amine drawings do not establish a physiological protonation state, exposure, or useful binding geometry.
missing_features: Matched stable connecting groups preserving the aryl/basic-amine arrangement are not established alongside the acid-chloride, aldehyde, and chloromethyl leaders.
The potentially stereogenic saturated-ring connections have no explicit stereochemical specification.
Ordinary ring alternatives preserving the late oxygen-bridged aromatic substitution pattern are missing from the cited final series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl-amino pyrrolidine/enamine/chloromethyl molecule scores 0.993896; its analogue lacking the aryl amino group scores 0.986744. An aldehyde-containing diaza-ring analogue scores 0.993273, and an acid-chloride/piperidine analogue scores 0.992660. A chloromethyl diaza-ring structure without the linking enamine nitrogen still reaches 0.988417, so no single reactive linkage is established as necessary. Conversely, a shortened monoaryl enamine carrying a fluorinated amidine scores 0.001971, and a biaryl carboxylic acid/acetamide scores 0.000719. The observed association is with the assembled aryl/basic-ring architecture and its connections, not aromaticity, nitrogen, or halogen presence alone. The current seed-1 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.951235 while changing from a bridged cage/aldehyde family to linked cyclic amines; the parent already reached roughly 0.991 in other seeds with different aryl-amine structures.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest current family is comparatively conventional: an N-aryl fused pyrrolidine-like ring and a cyclic dione/ureide region carry an ethoxyphenyl substituent and an alkyl-substituted phenyl or pyridyl group. Carbonyl acceptors and an NH coexist with a partly saturated ring and substantial aromatic surface. Other seeds retain expanded nitrogen/carbonyl rings, annulated aromatic systems, and lactone-like connections; occasional outputs join two such large systems. Ring and aromatic presence rates are 0.992 and 0.9862, but the halogen rate is only 0.1655. Mean SMILES length is 59.2. The leading family is more apparently synthesizable than many other task leaders because it avoids direct N-halogen bonds and exotic small-ring unsaturation, although a route and stereochemical identity remain unspecified.
liabilities: Multiple aromatic groups and alkyl/ethoxy substitution create a sizable hydrophobic surface; the trajectories do not establish solubility.
Late structures still contain difficult expanded polycycles, N-O connections, or duplicated ring systems.
The substituted saturated ring in the otherwise plausible leading family has unspecified stereochemistry.
missing_features: More independent, compact aryl/carbonyl arrangements are underrepresented relative to decoration of the same fused dione family.
Stereochemically specified substituted saturated rings are absent.
Matched simplifications of extended or repeated polycycles that preserve useful carbonyl and aryl relationships are not demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The alkylphenyl/ethoxyphenyl fused dione scores 0.229908; replacing one aryl carbon with nitrogen gives 0.229106, and expansion of the partly saturated ring gives 0.223627. Other changes to propyl, methyl, and ethoxy decoration produce nearby but lower scores, such as 0.221324 and 0.221171. This is a shallow preference among closely related complete aryl/carbonyl scaffolds. Methane, acetylene, and hydrogen peroxide score zero, while dimethyl ether scores 0.014932. A large doubled final polycycle scores 0.156670 versus 0.206435 for another, less repeated final polycycle; these are not matched structures, but size alone is plainly insufficient. The current seed-1 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.213370 and exchanges its N-fluorinated bridged dione for a more conventional fused dione. The parent's overall best was 0.224057 in a different expanded-ring family, so the current chemistry extends rather than resolves the modest score region.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact nitrogen-rich fused aromatic or partly saturated carbonyl/imino systems, usually with phenolic oxygen, N-methyl or fluoromethyl substitution, and fluorinated unsaturated small rings. The best has a cyclobutadiene-like substituent containing two double bonds in a small carbon ring. Other high-scoring structures contain fluorinated cyclopropenes, fused unsaturated small nitrogen rings, or direct N-F bonds. These are substantial chemical feasibility concerns despite moderate molecular size. The lowest-scoring structures instead combine multiple large aromatic dione systems through esters, carbonyls, or ring-to-ring connections. Aromatic and ring presence rates are 0.9471 and 0.977, with mean SMILES length 53.9; neither scarcity of aromatic rings nor simple failure to grow molecules explains the observed output.
liabilities: Cyclobutadiene-like unsaturation brings severe strain and electronic instability concerns.
Fluorinated cyclopropenes and fused unsaturated small heterocycles further constrain feasible geometry and synthesis.
Direct N-F substitution is chemically distinct from routine carbon-bound fluorination and introduces a separate reactivity concern.
Large repeated aromatic carbonyl structures remain present even where their supplied scores are extremely small.
missing_features: Conventional ring replacements retaining the leading carbonyl/imino and fluorinated substituent arrangement are absent among the cited leaders.
Matched stable alternatives to direct N-F substitution and highly unsaturated small rings are not established.
Compact, independently connected alternatives are poorly represented relative to fused-ring rearrangements or duplication of existing aromatic dione systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated fused imino/carbonyl leader scores 0.522447. Removing its aromatic fluorine while preserving the remaining depicted connectivity lowers the score to 0.486230, supporting a local substituent preference without demonstrating a general fluorination rule. Two different cyclopropene-bearing structures, one N-fluorinated and one bearing N-fluoromethyl, both score about 0.491792; their other topology differences prevent attributing the result solely to that substitution, and do not establish a need for N-F. Large repeated structures score as low as 3.48e-50, and a late joined fused-ring assembly scores 1.70e-12, indicating a strong observed disadvantage for those particular oversized combinations. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.407140 while introducing more unsaturated small-ring chemistry. The parent's seed-1 maximum was higher, 0.584558, in an aryl dione/aminomethyl/fluoromethyl family without these cyclobutadiene-like substituents, so the current score does not justify interpreting strain as chemically necessary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring outputs contain acid chlorides, aldehydes, alkyl halides, imidoyl halides, nitroso groups, direct nitrogen-halogen bonds, and unusual sulfur bonding. Other high-scoring structures omit individual liabilities, while the conventional aryl dione family demonstrates that reactive decorations are not universally required.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable functional-group alternatives are incompletely explored around otherwise productive molecular architectures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically stable replacements and removals accessible while preserving the surrounding ring connections, aryl placement, and approximate molecular size. Evaluate those alternatives through the current objective's own feedback rather than treating reactive groups in a leading molecule as required chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied molecules include cyclobutadiene-like substituents, fluorinated cyclopropenes, benzene-annulated unsaturated small rings, and tightly oxygen-bridged aromatic structures. Rich ring-token presence therefore coexists with substantial strain concerns; conventional fused diones and saturated amine rings are also available in the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction does not consistently preserve chemically credible unsaturation and geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide local changes to ring size, saturation, and fusion connectivity that preserve useful substituent relationships while allowing ordinary ring geometry. Ring closure and valence validity alone should not stand in for accessible chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One population has mean SMILES length 95.2 and maximum 227, with repeated dione assemblies. Several very large variants tie at 0.603906 despite shortening an unsaturated side chain, while other repeated assemblies have scores near zero. The same supplied trajectories also contain simple fragments after complete aromatic/carbonyl structures have been generated.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular size changes too often duplicate elaborate ring systems or remove most of the useful architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled simplification, removal of repeated units, and bounded connecting-group edits that retain a coherent molecular core. Let accepted structural comparisons determine useful size instead of assuming either growth or fragmentation is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports zero explicit tetrahedral stereolabel presence on every proposal population. Cited substituted saturated nitrogen rings, brominated side chains, and partly saturated fused diones contain stereogenic connectivity whose configurations are not specified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity unspecified even when it creates potentially stereogenic connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve known stereochemistry through structural edits and make valid local stereoisomer alternatives available when new centres arise. Use the current scoring feedback to determine whether stereochemical identity matters, without assuming that a label alone improves the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading aryl amides and diones have interpretable local analogues, including a near-tied phenyl/pyridyl pair and a lower-scoring sulfur-cumulene analogue. Elsewhere, changes simultaneously alter ring topology, heteroatom connection, reactive decoration, and size, leaving high scores attached to chemically questionable whole structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many nominally distinct molecules provide limited information about which stable structural feature is responsible for a score difference.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand matched local alternatives that isolate aryl position, heteroatom placement, carbonyl connection, and ring saturation while retaining the remainder of the molecule. Combine this with access to independently connected, synthetically credible scaffolds rather than only repeated decoration of the current ring family.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
